prize_parts.citation: For the theoretical prediction of the quantum spin Hall state and the Z2 topological classification of insulators, and for the first experimental observation of protected edge transport in HgTe quantum wells.

statement.case_for: I keep B041 with Kane, Mele and Molenkamp, unchanged from round 1. Band topology is now an organising principle well beyond electrons in solids (photonics, cold atoms, mechanical systems), which is the kind of conceptual reach I look for as a theorist of complex systems. The Kane-Mele paper supplies the Z2 classification and the quantum spin Hall proposal, and Molenkamp's HgTe quantum wells supplied a direct transport fingerprint (quantised edge conductance). The prize therefore rests on a prediction that was observed. More than fifteen years of independent confirmation by transport, ARPES and scanning probes make the interpretation stable. The chair's question about the third slot does not move me: the Z2 theory is a joint Kane-Mele contribution, so omitting Mele would split one theoretical origin, and a citation tied to the quantum spin Hall state and Z2 classification matches exactly these three names. Round 1 produced no new argument that makes me prefer another configuration. On the 2016 prize, Thouless, Haldane and Kosterlitz honoured topological phase transitions and topological phases in low-dimensional systems; what is new here is the time-reversal-protected Z2 class in a material with strong spin-orbit coupling, and its experimental realisation. I regard that as distinct, though not trivially so.
statement.case_against: The credit problem is not solved by any three-name choice. Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang predicted the HgTe quantum spin Hall state that Molenkamp's group observed, and Fu, Moore, Balents and Roy are central to the 3D theory; none can be named under the limit, and Zhang's death complicates any argument about the first. Hasan's ARPES work is a real independent experimental claim. A citation that leans on the 2D chain is honest about its scope but will read as incomplete to part of the community. The 2016 prize also leaves a legitimate question of overlap: some members may judge that the conceptual step was already rewarded. B013 is the strongest rival. Its attribution is cleaner and its consequences are testable, and Kroll argues well for it. My view is that B041 is the larger reorganisation of the field, but I accept that this is a judgment about criteria and not a settled fact.

responses.point: Kane, Molenkamp and Hasan would credit theory, the first 2D experiment and the first 3D materials, with a citation reaching to three-dimensional topological materials.
responses.response: I still disagree with the trade, though I take the 3D case seriously. Replacing Mele with Hasan removes half of the joint Kane-Mele theory in order to add a third experimental claim, and your own acknowledgement that Mele's omission separates a joint contribution weakens the configuration. A citation that reaches 3D materials also pulls in Fu, Moore, Balents and Roy, which no three names can cover, so it invites a harder dispute than the 2D one. If the committee prefers the wider framing, I would want the argument made on the ground that the 3D materials are the discovery's main legacy, not on the ground that experiment needs two slots.

responses.point: B013 is a compact invention with concrete tests (about 1e-18 accuracy, geodesy, constants, dark matter), and if conceptual reorganisation is judged to outweigh instrumental invention, B041 is the more defensible choice.
responses.response: I think your own conditional answers the chair's last question, and I accept the framing: the deciding criterion is whether a discovery reorganised how a community thinks, and I judge that B041 does so more broadly. I do not dismiss B013, since the attribution is cleaner than in B041 and part of the case is a redefinition of the second that has not yet happened. That makes the measurement case partly prospective, while topological insulators have fifteen years of confirmation behind them. I also note that you flagged a possible conflict through the Hall group, which the committee should settle if B013 became the main contender.

responses.point: Kane-Mele-Molenkamp is the cleanest theory-plus-experiment pairing, but the 2016 prize covers part of the conceptual background, and the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang HgTe prediction must be addressed.
responses.response: I agree on the configuration and share the 2016 concern. My answer is that the 2016 prize rewarded topological transitions and phases in low dimensions, whereas this work introduced Z2 invariants for time-reversal-symmetric insulators and the observation of protected edge transport, so it is new. On Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang, I think the citation should describe the quantum spin Hall state and its first observation in HgTe without claiming the quantum-well prediction, which keeps it accurate. That does not remove the omission, and I would want the committee to say so openly.

responses.point: B013 is a single sharp invention with testable downstream consequences, and Ye's inclusion in B007 could affect how clock credit is framed.
responses.response: I accept that atomic clocks answer a real criterion, and I withdraw my earlier doubt about whether an instrument counts as a discovery. My remaining worry is practical: a combined B041 and B013 prize would need five names, which the limit forbids, and cutting B041 to two would drop Mele or Molenkamp and weaken its attribution. I would therefore support B013 as a later prize, and I do not read the sequencing question as an argument against B041 now.

uncertainties: Whether Mele or Hasan should hold the third slot remains a matter of judgment; I cannot settle it from the supplied text.
Whether the 2016 prize is felt to have covered the area, which would weaken B041.
How the citation should treat Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang, Fu, Moore and Balents, who cannot be credited.
Whether B029 (Xue's quantum anomalous Hall realisation) is a separate achievement; I treat it as part of the same story.
My knowledge of the priority history is from recollection and not verified against sources.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile: none of the credited names for B041 or the alternatives appears among my documented collaborators or supervisors. I note Kroll's possible conflict on B013 and would defer to the committee's handling of it.
